title: "PBS: Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme"
description: "Information about medicines provided to people under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme."

Information about medicines provided to people under the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme.

*Explains the medicine subsidy program and links to listings, statistics and supporting information.*

The PBS specification is explicit that the prescriber's location \"is based on the postcode of the location at which the prescriber performed the majority of Medicare services for the most recent relevant quarter\", which is what the MJR token in the name records. It is therefore a property of the doctor over a quarter rather than of the prescribing event on the row. PRSCRBR_ID_SCRAM says which prescriber wrote the script, and PRSCRBR_TYP_CD and MJR_SPCLTY_GRP_CD say what kind of practitioner they are.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the prescriber location and remoteness items","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Prescriber postcode","k":"Australian postcode","def":"A four-digit Australian postcode from the same domain as the patient and pharmacy postcodes on the row, with values drawn from the Postcode datafile behind METeOR data element 611398.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific notes on the prescriber location and remoteness items","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","lim":"It cannot place a prescription geographically. METeOR defines it as \"the total number of times that the prescribed medicinal product is supplied to the patient or PBS consumer\", and sets the rule that a repeat prescription takes \"a value of 1 for those prescriptions where Regulation 24 applicable indicator has a negative response, or a value equivalent to 1 plus the number of repeats specified by the prescriber\" where that indicator is positive. It rises above 1 only on the Regulation 24 rows, where the original and all its repeats went out together. Counting rows counts supply events; summing this column counts the supplies bundled inside them.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 605072, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—number of authorised medication supplies, total number N[N]' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/605072","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Number of authorised medication supplies","k":"count of supplies","def":"A whole number in METeOR's format N[N], two characters at most, with 99 reserved for not stated or inadequately described. The PBS specification says the underlying field is the patient's date of birth and that \"'Patient date of birth' is extracted from the Medicare record of the patient, as reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)\", which PLIDA splits into this column and PTNT_BRTH_YR. Taken with the year it fixes age at supply to within a month, which is what age-group analyses of dispensing rest on. It describes the person the medicine was supplied to, not the prescriber and not whoever paid.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Month of birth","k":"month of year, 1 to 12","def":"A month number from 1 to 12, carrying the month component of METeOR's date of birth element (287007), whose full domain is DDMMYYYY. The PBS specification says of the underlying field that it \"can be used to identify individual patients and may, in some use cases, need to be suppressed or perturbed\", which is why only a year and a month survive here, and that it \"is extracted from the Medicare record of the patient, as reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)\". Subtracting it from the year of SPPLY_DT gives age at supply to within a year, and PTNT_BRTH_MTH tightens that to a month. It is the patient's year of birth, not the year they came onto Medicare.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient date of birth item","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Year of birth","k":"calendar year","def":"A four-digit calendar year, the year component of METeOR's DDMMYYYY date of birth element (287007). METeOR defines it as \"the total amount paid by the patient or PBS consumer to the approved pharmacy for a prescription, exclusive of any special patient contributions, e.g. brand price premiums or therapeutic group premiums\", and adds that the amount \"also excludes any optional fees imposed at the discretion of the pharmacy and payable by the patient\". The value moves with the patient's entitlement rather than with the medicine, so it is set by PTNT_CTGRY_DRVD_CD and by whether the Safety Net threshold had been reached that calendar year. With BNFT_AMT it splits the dispensed price between the patient and the Commonwealth.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 603362, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—PBS patient contribution, total Australian currency N[NNNNN].NN' (Department of Health)","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603362","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Patient contribution amount","k":"Australian currency amount, dollars and cents","def":"Australian currency to two decimal places, in METeOR's format N[NNNNN].NN. The value tracks the co-payment published in the Schedule of Pharmaceutical Benefits, which METeOR says is adjusted each 1 January in line with the CPI, although statute has since frozen the concessional rate at $7.70 for 2025 to 2029: METeOR gives $36.90 for a general patient and $6.00 for a concessional patient in 2014, and the schedule's fee table gave $25.00 and $7.70 as at 1 July 2026.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data element 603362, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) prescription—PBS patient contribution, total Australian currency N[NNNNN].NN' (Department of Health)","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/603362","lim":"It is not the money that left the patient's pocket. Brand price premiums, therapeutic group premiums and any discretionary pharmacy fee are excluded by definition, so a patient who chose a premium brand paid more than this column shows. It is also not a basis for a consistent affordability series over the whole 2006 to 2025 span, because supplies priced below the general co-payment were not collected at all until April 2012.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_CTGRY_DRVD_CD","d":"Patient entitlement status (derived)","vp":"ai","od":"Patient entitlement status (derived)","k":"pbs_patient_entitlement_status_derived","def":"The source publishes this value domain of 9 values. The PBS specification says the derived patient state \"is derived from 'Patient postcode', i.e. it is derived from the Medicare record of the patient and is based on the most recent patient address reported to the Department of Human Services (DHS)\", and this column is that postcode. It is the geography every patient-side analysis of PBS rests on, including the remoteness categories the department publishes. Set against PHRMCY_PSTCD it shows whether the script was filled near home.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient state item","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Patient postcode","k":"Australian postcode","def":"A four-digit Australian postcode. METeOR's general Australian postcode domain (data element 611398) sources values from the Postcode datafile and reserves 0097, 0098 and 0099 for not applicable, unknown and not stated.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data set specification 602524, 'Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) state/territory data extract 2013-14' (Department of Health), DSS specific note on the patient state item","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602524","lim":"Medicare holds one current address rather than an address history, so an old value can be stamped on a recent supply and a move stays invisible until the person tells Services Australia. The postcode also belongs to an enrolment rather than to a residence: a child on a parent's record carries the parent's postcode, and someone living away for study or care may carry a family address. For an actual residential history the address episodes in Core Locations, keyed by ARID, are the source.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"PTNT_SEX_CD","d":"The patient's sex as the Medicare entitlement record held it at the moment the claim was archived.","full":"The patient's sex as the Medicare entitlement record held it at the moment the claim was archived. METeOR's PBS note is explicit that \"this data item is defined as being 'the gender of the consumer as held in the entitlement tables at the time the PBS claim was archived'\", and warns that \"gender is a social/cultural concept rather than a biological (anatomical or chromosomal) concept, although for most people the two concepts are the same\". It belongs to the patient the medicine was supplied to, not to the prescriber or the cardholder. With PTNT_BRTH_YR it gives the two demographic splits available on a PBS row without leaving the table.","dsrc":"AIHW METeOR data element 602450, 'Person—sex, code A' (Department of Health), with the PBS specific note recorded against it","durl":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602450","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Patient sex","k":"sex code","def":"A one-character alphabetic code from METeOR's Sex code A domain, covering male, female, and intersex or indeterminate, with separate supplementary codes for not stated or inadequately described and for unknown, and a blank also read as unknown.","p":"2006 to 2025","s":"sourced","src":"AIHW METeOR data element 602450, 'Person—sex, code A' (Department of Health), with the PBS specific note recorded against it","url":"https://meteor.aihw.gov.au/content/602450","lim":"It is a point-in-time administrative value, so a person whose Medicare record changed will carry different codes on rows before and after the change and a person-level mode will quietly erase that. It is also not comparable with the sex and gender items in Census, surveys or birth records, which are self-reported against different questions, so a disagreement between PBS and Census is not by itself evidence of a bad link.","where":["madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_6","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_7","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_8","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2006 / pbs_2006_9","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_1","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_10","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_11","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_12","madipge-pbs-d-prescriptions-2007 / pbs_2007_2","and 220 more"]},{"n":"RGLTN24_IND","d":"Whether the pharmacist was allowed to hand over the original script and all its repeats at once.","full":"Whether the pharmacist was allowed to hand over the original script and all its repeats at once. METeOR defines it as \"an indicator of whether supply of the original Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) item and all repeats is made at the one time\", under a regulation that \"allows a pharmacist to supply an original prescription medication and all of its repeats at the one time\", and restricts such prescriptions to medical practitioners, midwives and nurse practitioners.
